answer: A skill-ladder gate admits an identity after three rungs bound to one key. At the jetty intake it posts 20, then 40 and 80 at rungs two and three: 140 locked per identity. A failed audit burns the bond; a reused sample fails the hash check, so one ladder cannot be copied across keys. The ridge checkpoint re-grades rung three, and a haven list pays only graduates. The kth fake identity pays 140, so 1,000 cost 140,000 credits, unmerged. Renting a ladder fails, as progress is key-bound and a transferred key restarts at rung one. An honest agent climbs once for 140 credits.
